Israel deadlocked: Do the Arabs hold the key to defeating Netanyahu?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:48:26 UTC
04:48:26 KST

Netanyahu’s Israel deadlocked: were the elections ‘stolen by the Arabs’?
Israel’s parliamentary elections are over, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been wounded, but not defeated. His battle to form a government and stay in power is just beginning.
The final results of the Israeli election won’t be known until Thursday, when Israel’s Central Election Committee (CEC) finishes tallying so-called ‘double envelope’ ballots cast by soldiers, diplomats living abroad, prisoners, and other voters unable to make it to polling stations on election day.
However, with more than 85% of votes counted as of Wednesday evening, a picture of political deadlock is becoming clearer, and neither Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc, nor the center-left to center-right bloc of his opponents, are on track to win a majority in the Israeli parliament, the Knesset. Either bloc must secure 61 out of 120 Knesset seats to form a government.
What are the results of the Israeli election?
Netanyahu’s Likud remains Israel’s largest political party, and is projected to win 26 seats, down from 32 in 2022.
Yashar, led by Netanyahu’s chief rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is in second place with 21 seats.
Both politicians lead large and potentially fractious blocs. Together with four far-right and religious parties – Otzma Yehudit, United Torah Judaism, Shas, and Religious Zionism, Netanyahu’s bloc controls 53 seats, ten short of a majority.
Eisenkot’s opposition bloc comprises Yashar, former Prime Ministers’ Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid’s B’Yachad party, Yair Golan’s Democrats, and Yisrael Beytenu, a right-wing party led by former Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman. Together, this bloc controls 48 seats.
What about the Arabs?
Israel’s two main Arab parties, Yousef Jabareen’s Joint List and Mansour Abbas’ Ra’am, have almost doubled their representation in the Knesset. Driven by anger over Netanyahu’s war on Gaza and his appointment of overt Jewish supremacists to cabinet positions, voters in Arab-majority districts turned out in record numbers to award the Joint List and Ra’am 12 and seven seats respectively, up from a combined ten seats in 2022.
With a combined 19 seats, the Arab parties could play the role of kingmakers when coalition talks begin. However, they would likely find few allies within either Jewish-led bloc.
Will Netanyahu work with the Arabs?
Netanyahu has explicitly ruled out cooperation with either Arab party, both of which have condemned his war on Gaza. “It is forbidden, simply forbidden, to endanger Israel and to establish a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties,” he said after polls closed on Tuesday.
In the run up to the vote, the Israeli prime minister framed the election as a choice between “Me and [US President Donald] Trump, or Eisenkot and Abbas,” and accused his opponents of plotting to recognize a Palestinian state after entering a government with the Arabs.
In a statement on Wednesday, Netanyahu claimed that “the elections in the State of Israel were stolen by Arab parties,” and that Likud had uncovered evidence of vote-buying, “threats and violence against polling station members,” and repeat voting in Arab districts. The PM called on police and Israel’s Shin Bet intelligence agency to conduct a “thorough investigation” into his claims.
Eisenkot’s party warned on Tuesday that Netanyahu would attempt to delegitimize the election. “Netanyahu is panicking and has begun making up stories and claiming that the election is being stolen,” Yashar said in a statement. “This is no accident. He is already laying the groundwork to challenge the election results.”
What about the opposition?
Eisenkot, Liberman, and Bennett have all ruled out cooperation with the Arabs, with Eisenkot declaring on election night that he intends to form “a Zionist government.” Democrats leader Yair Golan, on the other hand, has called on the anti-Netanyahu bloc to reach out to Ra’am and the Joint List for the sake of ousting Netanyau. Partnership with the two Arab parties would give the bloc 65 seats – a clear majority.
“We have no future here if we don’t stop being afraid,” he wrote on social media on Wednesday morning. “We have a majority. We have responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel’s Arab citizens.”
Abbas has said that he is willing to enter government with the anti-Netanyahu bloc, while Jabareen has said that his Joint List lawmakers would “pave the way for the ousting of the Netanyahu government” by refusing to oppose a minority government in exchange for some concessions on Palestine and funding for Arab communities.
Who will form a government in Israel?
Israeli President Isaac Herzog will ultimately decide which political leader stands the best chance of forming a stable government, and task them with forming a coalition. Herzog has called on all parties to enter negotiations “with an open mind.” As the political horse-trading begins, three potential outcomes are laid out below:
Netanyahu wins back the right
Netanyahu could secure a majority by striking a deal with Bennett and Liberman to peel B’Yachad away from the opposition bloc. Both are right-wingers, but both campaigned on ousting Netanyahu and forcing military conscription on Israel’s ultra-Orthodox Haredi communities. In this case,, Netanyahu would likely lose the backing of the two ultra-Orthodox parties in his coalition, United Torah Judaism and Shas.
Swapping these parties for B’Yachad would leave Netanyahu’s bloc even further away from a majority, meaning one side would have to compromise on their core campaign promises to make this arrangement work.
Eisenkot joins the Arabs
Eisenkot’s opposition bloc could quickly secure a majority and form a government, but only if he, Bennett, and Liberman decide that taking power is worth cooperating with, or securing the abstention of, the Arab parties.
Doing so would carry political consequences for everyone involved. At a time when public support for a two-state solution has collapsed and fewer Israelis than ever believe that they “cannot coexist peacefully” with their Palestinian neighbors, Eisenkot, Bennett, and Liberman would risk alienating their right-wing voters.
Likewise, Arab voters could see any partnership with the Israeli-right as a betrayal by the Joint List and Ra’am. Earlier this week, Joint List parliamentary leader Ahmad Tibi alluded to this fear, telling Türkiye’s Anadolu news agency that he does not want his party “to be responsible for incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque, a war in Gaza, the continuation of Jewish terrorism and settlement activity, or house demolitions.”
Entering a government with Eisenkot and the right-wing opposition would make the Joint List “collectively responsible” for these crimes, he explained.
Could a grand Zionist coalition emerge in Israel?
A unity government – in which Netanyahu and Eisenkot rotate the premiership with the support of Bennett and Liberman – may seem like an obvious solution for everyone involved. Likud, Yashar, B’Yachad, and Yisrael Beytenu are all aligned on security matters, and entering a grand coalition would allow Netanyahu to cast off his ultra-Orthodox and far-right partners, while Eisenkot could sever ties with the Democrats and Arabs.
Such an arrangement is not without precedent. In 2020, Netanyahu and Benny Gantz – a centrist ex-general – reached a power-sharing agreement after three elections in less than a year.
However, the Netanyahu/Gantz coalition fell apart in less than a year, at a less polarized time in Israeli politics. This time around, all of Netanyahu’s opponents have focused their campaigns around deposing the prime minister, with Eisenkot accusing him of corruption, incompetence, and ignoring “dozens of warnings” prior to Hamas’ attack on Israel in 2023.
“I unequivocally pledge that I will not serve under Netanyahu in a rotation agreement. Period,” Eisenkot told Radio 103 last week. “If that were to happen, you would see me resign an hour later.” Eisenkot did not explicitly rule out working with Likud, if Netanyahu were to retire.
The alternative for Israel: deadlock and elections
Should none of these arrangements work, Israel could be thrust into another election cycle. Repeat elections and failed coalition talks were a leitmotif in Israeli politics until the October 7 attack and subsequent wars ushered in a period of relative stability: in the four years before 2022, Israel went through five elections.
Herzog has made it clear that he wants to avoid such an outcome. “We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” he said on Tuesday. However, unless Israel’s main parties can find some kind of compromise, another election may be inevitable.

Colombia's lower house rejects changes to pension reform articles
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:45:59 UTC
04:45:59 KST

Colombia's lower house rejects changes to pension reform articles
BOGOTA, Oct 28 - Colombia's lower house on Wednesday rejected changes to a package of specific articles from a pension reform bill that had been returned to the legislature by the Constitutional Court, which ordered lawmakers to remedy a procedural flaw in the bill.
In August, the Constitutional Court approved most of the 2024 pension system reform, championed by former President Gustavo Petro.
The rejection means the version of the bill approved by the Senate will stand and the court will now need to decide if the procedural flaw has been corrected.
The pension reform aims to strengthen the state-run pension administrator Colpensiones, reduce subsidies for high pensions, provide benefits to women with children, and expand coverage to protect older adults living in poverty.
The bill maintains the retirement age at 62 for men and 57 for women. The law requires all Colombians earning up to 2.3 times the monthly minimum wage — approximately 4 million pesos (about $1,300) — to make contributions to Colpensiones.
Those earning above that amount can choose a private pension fund for the surplus portion of their income.
The measure also stipulates that workers who failed to accumulate enough contribution weeks to qualify for a pension will receive aid, while those in poverty who did not contribute will receive a monthly payment of around $75.
The Petro government estimated more than 2.6 million older adults will benefit from the measures.
Men with 900 weeks of contributions and women with 750 will remain in the current system and will not be required to contribute to the state fund.
Some economic and social initiatives championed by Petro were rejected or faced difficulties gaining approval in Congress, where he lacked solid support. He left office in August and was replaced by right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who has pledged to maintain some of Petro's popular social reforms.
The reform is one of Colombia’s most significant social policy reforms in years, according to analysts, who note that it would expand the state’s role in the pension system while preserving a role for private funds—an issue that has long divided lawmakers, businesses, and unions. REUTERS

====================================================================================================

Fed holds rates steady despite concerns over inflation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:43:48 UTC
04:43:48 KST

The Federal Reserve voted Wednesday to keep benchmark interest rates on hold, opting to take a patient approach in its fight against inflation despite mounting evidence that price pressures are proving more nettlesome than policymakers had hoped.
In a widely expected decision, the Federal Open Market Committee kept the overnight funds rate in a range between 3.75%-4%, where it has been since the central bank approved a quarter percentage point increase in September.
"Inflation remains elevated," the post-meeting statement said. "The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability."
Two voters dissented
Two of the 12 FOMC voters dissented from the decision – Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, both of whom wanted the committee to raise rates by a quarter percentage point.
Cook has been at the center of a continuing controversy in which President Donald Trump has tried to remove her from office over allegations concerning information she provided on home loan applications. While the Supreme Court stopped the president's attempts, the administration has restarted the move, with a hearing scheduled for early November.
This was Cook's first dissent since joining the Fed in 2022 as an appointee of President Joe Biden.
Dallas President Lorie Logan and Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari both joined Hammack in voting no the last time the committee held, in July, and both have expressed the need for higher rates. However, they fell in with the majority Wednesday.
The midterm elections have lingered over the decision. Pivotal votes take place nationwide on Nov. 3, with control of Congress at stake. Fed officials consider political independence to be a cornerstone of the central bank, but some observers have speculated that officials won't want to raise rates this close to an election.
Trump, who nominated Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to the position, has been at odds with the Fed for years. Trump has charged that the funds rate should be much lower.
The dissents reflected underlying conflict on the committee over how aggressively it needs to raise rates to combat rising prices. Inflation has been above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years, and the pace of price increases has only picked up since the September meeting.
Statements over the past several weeks, though, have reflected a desire to wait for additional data to come in before tightening policy further. Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams both said current economic conditions allow policymakers time to evaluate their next move.
The statement characterized economic activity as "expanding at a strong pace," a seeming upgrade from "solid" in September. There were no other substantial changes to the statement other than the removal of a sentence that explained the September increase.
The decision came as little surprise as markets had been pricing in a less than 10% chance of a hike, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. Following the decision, the S&P 500 held on to its gains.
However, it raises fresh questions about how long policymakers are willing to wait before tightening again. Futures market pricing indicates a strong possibility of another hike at the next FOMC meeting in December, and perhaps another increase or two in 2027.
Separately, Warsh unveiled at a news conference changes to the FOMC meetings next year that could reduce the number of rate-setting meetings each year.
"We believe eight meetings per year is the right number for the FOMC, but in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated," Warsh said. "The rest will be regular FOMC policy setting meetings, and I expect that in 2028 we'll have two meetings dedicated discussions of strategy and six for setting policy."
Complicated economic picture
The Fed is up against a complicated economic and political picture. Inflation as measured by the Fed's preferred gauge is expected to be above 3% for September, even when excluding volatile food and energy prices. Economists are concerned that inflation has broadened beyond the energy sector and the impact from the Iran war.
At the same time, the unemployment rate has remained low and economic growth has been strong. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow tracker is pointing to 3.4% annualized growth in the third quarter, which would be the strongest in a year. Consumer spending also has been solid, and investment tied to the artificial intelligence boom has helped keep the U.S. economic engine running.
The combination, though, has added to debate about how much restriction the Fed's current interest rate is actually exerting on the economy, and whether policymakers will need to move more aggressively if the price data doesn't improve.
While markets expect additional hikes, Warsh has avoided providing so-called forward guidance about the FOMC's intentions. In June, his fellow committee members, through the "dot plot" grid, indicated the likelihood of another increase this year.
"The Fed is taking a wait-and-see approach, and I think that makes sense given where we are in the cycle," said Andrew Davis, head of investment strategy at Bryn Mawr Trust and a former BLS analyst. "The economy is slowing, but slowing and breaking are two different things. Holding rates steady gives policymakers more time to assess how the economy is responding to September's hike and the recent rise in longer-term borrowing costs."

RFK, Jr.,  loosens restrictions for six popular peptides, bypassing the FDA
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:40:43 UTC
04:40:43 KST

The Department of Health and Human Services announced a loosening of restrictions on six unproven peptides on Wednesday. These substances have long been touted by biohackers as a means to hack people’s bodies and brains for the better, but they often have had scant scientific evidence behind them. In the past, HHS chief Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., has voiced support for peptides, such as the so-called Wolverine stack, a combination of two such substances—BPC-157 and TB-500—that is meant to promote healing. Both of these peptides are included in the list of those that are now available to dispense.
The new policy allows some licensed pharmacists to produce compounds made up of multiple peptides—provided that those peptides are made by registered manufacturers. Users must also have a valid prescription to receive the compounds.
In a document outlining the new policy, the agency acknowledged that compounded drugs carry risks: they are not regulated in the same way as a name-brand or generic medication by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, leading to concerns over their safety and efficacy. But the agency said that the level of public interest and available data had led it to expand access to some combinations of peptides and that doing so would discourage the growing gray and black markets for peptides.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Peptides are small chains of amino acids, which are the building blocks of proteins. Humans produce a large number of peptides naturally, but taking them as supplements has become a major trend among health influencers, tech executives and the “Make America Healthy Again” movement. Depending on the peptide, the substances are marketed as helping with everything from extending lifespan to healing from injuries and workouts to improving one’s complexion. Perhaps the best-known peptide products on the market are glucagonlike peptide 1 (GLP-1) drugs, such as Ozempic and Mounjaro.
The peptides included under the new policy are: BPC-157 and TB-500; Epitalon, which is promoted as a sleep and longevity aid; KPV, which is used as an anti-inflammatory; MOTS-c, which is used for obesity and osteoporosis; and Semax, a supplement for migraine and chronic pain.
Willie Underwood III, president of the American Medical Association, criticized the policy shift in a statement, saying the peptides have "not undergone the rigorous testing required of FDA-approved drugs."
"“Allowing pharmacies to compound unapproved synthetic peptide substances without sufficient evidence of their safety and efficacy puts patients at risk," he said. "Expanding access without adequate safeguards and oversight could expose patients to serious, preventable harm.”
The affected peptides are also rarely taken alone, and in some cases, there is very little research as to what so-called stacks of two or more peptides might do to health. Despite that lack of evidence, the loosening of restrictions has come after the FDA began analyzing how to make the substances more accessible and convened a panel to discuss allowing compounding pharmacies to manufacture them.
HHS appeared to acknowledge the lack of data in its announcement, saying it may revisit the issue if safety or product quality issues arise as the compounded peptides become more available.
Editor’s Note (10/28/26): This is a breaking news story and may be updated.

Spain high-speed train crash kills 68
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:40:43 UTC
04:40:43 KST

Spain high-speed train crash kills 68
A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said, in one of Europe's deadliest such disasters this century.
The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country's rail safety, with the transport minister speaking of an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to the collision.
AFP reporters on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha saw one train embedded into another and some carriages lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment.
Dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour.
Castilla-La Mancha's leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene that 68 people had died, raising an earlier toll of 64 and having already warned of more victims being found.
A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha regional government told AFP that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition.
State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo.
Pablo Mejia, 42, with blood staining his grey jumper, told AFP that he had miraculously survived after changing his seat, as he awaited a transfer to the southern city of Seville.
He recounted "a very strong hit. It lasted a long time until it stopped, lots of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos."
A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz who lives in the village of Urda close to the site of the accident, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car.
Ortiz, 49, described a "horrific, horrible" scene that "smelled of an accident, of metal".
Transport Minister Oscar Puente told reporters that the collision came after a train was ordered to go in "error" despite a technical failure affecting the automatic control system that halted all services on a 69-kilometre stretch of track.
"The decision to resume traffic, while that system had not been restored, belongs to the control centre," which resumed traffic "in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable", Puente said.
The Renfe train restarted and travelled 25 kilometres until it collided with the stationary Iryo, at a speed that could have reached "up to 200 kilometres per hour", Puente added.
The control centre "had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it", Puente said.
The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year's first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29.
He said Spain would observe three days of mourning from Thursday, conceding it was "not acceptable" that two high-speed collisions could happen within months. His Socialists halted campaign activities.
The leader of the main opposition conservative Popular Party, Alberto Nunez Feijoo, who leads in most polls, also suspended campaigning but said: "Spain has the right to know what is going on with its infrastructure."
Condolences flooded in from across Spain and Europe. The Spanish royal household said on X it was "shocked and concerned" by the accident, conveying its support to the victims, their loved ones and the emergency services.
Spain's high-speed rail network has received huge investment in recent years, growing to become the second-largest in the world after China's and a source of national pride.
But Wednesday's accident comes after another collision between two high-speed trains outside the southern village of Adamuz in January left 46 dead, which raised major questions about safety on the country's railways.
That crash was Spain's deadliest train accident since 2013, when 80 people died after a train veered off a curved section of track outside the northwestern city of Santiago de Compostela.

'Reverse course while there's still time' — US senator tells ships carrying Russian diesel to turn around
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:40:00 UTC
04:40:00 KST

'Reverse course while there's still time' — US senator tells ships carrying Russian diesel to turn around
U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat, issued a warning to the shipping company transporting a cargo of Russian diesel to the United States: turn back, or risk violating U.S. sanctions law.
The senator's demand comes a few days after Reuters reported that the Malta-flagged tanker Agioi Fanendes was heading to New York with 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel — the first delivery under a recent deal announced by U.S. President Donald Trump.
Blumenthal penned a letter to Athanasios Martinos, managing director of the shipping service Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Limited, urging him to confirm the reports and recall the vessel.
"I'm sending a sledgehammer message to shipping companies whose tankers are transporting illegal Russian diesel to our ports," Blumenthal said in a social media message accompanying the letter. "Reverse course while there's still time."
The letter points out that diesel shipments are banned under the 2022 Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act, signed into law by former President Joe Biden following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
"Should the Agioi Fanendes port and discharge its cargo, you would be engaged in an illegal transaction or aiding and abetting it," he warns.
Trump's diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin —announced Oct. 9, with the stated goal of bringing down domestic fuel prices — does not "supersede clear, unambiguous law," the letter argues.
"The Administration's conflicting directives on Russian energy in the past weeks should not be used as an excuse to ignore legal prohibitions," Blumenthal writes. "The President may have given a license to facilitate this transaction, but only Congress can make it legally valid."
read also
Blumenthal's letter is part of a wave of legislative action against Trump's diesel deal, which has provoked strong bipartisan backlash.
Previously, the Kyiv Independent reported that Democratic officials have been contacting U.S. industries involved in facilitating the deal to ensure they understood the potential legal and investigative risks.
U.S. Representative Gregory Meeks, a Democrat and ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, introduced the Prohibit Corrupt Russia Oil Deals Act, a bill designed to block imports of Russian diesel and mandate further sanctions against Moscow.
But as Congress looks to block the deal, the Agioi Fanendes is making its way to the U.S. East Coast. The ship loaded its cargo in the Russian Baltic port of Primorsk on Oct. 22 and is set to arrive in the U.S. on Nov. 7.
When announcing the deal, Trump claimed Russia would "immediately supply over 300,000" metric tons of diesel fuel to U.S. and global markets, delivering 500,000 metric tons in November and 1 million metric tons "immediately thereafter."
Soon after the announcement, Moscow partially lifted restrictions on its diesel exports, permitting the sale of 500,000 metric tons.
The deal shocked Kyiv, European partners, and U.S. lawmakers, who argued the move would help Putin finance the war in Ukraine without having to make any substantial concessions. Russian diesel imports are also unlikely to do much to offset domestic gas prices, which have primarily been driven up by the war against Iran.

A group of countries including the US, the UK, Japan as well as the EU on Wednesday reiterated their demand for North Korea to abandon its nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs and urged all UN member states to fully implement sanctions.

"The MSMT and EU reaffirm our commitment to the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the DPRK, calling on it to abandon its unlawful WMD and ballistic missile programs, and taking action to counter DPRK attempts to violate and evade UN sanctions."
It added: "We continue to strongly support the implementation of all DPRK-related UN Security Council resolutions."
The signatories also urged all UN member states, especially permanent members of the Security Council, to fully implement the resolutions.

Black Sea Drone Attack Near Bulgaria: 18 Crew Rescued as Hazardous Containers Drift

Bulgaria Has EU’s Highest Road Death Rate
Bulgaria recorded the European Union’s highest road fatality rate in 2025, with 71 deaths per million inhabitants, according to final figures released by the European Commission
The 18 crew members of the Liberian-flagged container ship CONTSHIP JET were rescued after three maritime drones struck the vessel in the Black Sea, while more than 20 containers containing hazardous materials drifted at sea, Bulgarian authorities and maritime news outlet Maritime.bg reported.
The ship was attacked at around noon about 16 nautical miles east of Cape Kaliakra, outside Bulgaria’s territorial waters but within its contiguous zone. According to Commander of the Naval Forces Rear Admiral Kiril Mihaylov, a French Navy Atlantique patrol aircraft monitoring the Black Sea first detected two unmanned surface vessels about 30 nautical miles east of Cape Kaliakra, followed by a third approximately 50 nautical miles away.
The drones were moving west toward several vessels passing through the area north of Cape Kaliakra, Mihaylov said. Information about the threat was immediately passed to maritime traffic control authorities, who were asked to warn ships in the area. The French aircraft also broadcast warnings over Channel 16 and continued tracking the drones, while updates were relayed through the French maritime command for the Mediterranean and Black Sea.
The first strike on the CONTSHIP JET occurred at approximately noon, followed by two more attacks. After a French aircraft reported that the crew was abandoning the vessel, the Naval Forces launched a search and rescue operation. Three naval vessels took part, and all 18 crew members had been rescued by 1:45 p.m., according to the Defense Ministry.
The ship remains afloat at the site of the attack and is drifting. Mihaylov said the vessel sustained three breaches on its port side, with the drones approaching from the east and hitting the western side. He credited the warning given to the crew with helping ensure that everyone survived.
"The crew was warned, which I believe played a crucial role in ensuring there were no casualties and that everyone was rescued," Mihaylov said.
The admiral declined to identify where the drones had originated, saying their point of departure was unknown. He said they had been detected in the area and that the third drone was the farthest away. The vessels approached at approximately 26 knots, he added.
Around 20 containers fell from the ship, prompting the Naval Forces to issue timely notices to mariners. Maritime.bg subsequently reported that more than 20 containers were drifting in the Black Sea and warned that they posed a hazard to navigation. A notice to mariners said the containers held "flammable gases, non-toxic non-flammable gases, flammable liquids, and other hazardous substances."
According to the ship’s captain, the cargo included various fuels and other hazardous materials. The Environment and Water Ministry later listed lithium-ion batteries, corrosive liquids and acids, flammable liquids including ethanol solutions, household chemicals and plastics, alongside food products, construction materials, timber, machinery and industrial components.
Mihaylov said the response window had been extremely short and that no assets or forces were close enough to intercept and destroy the drones in time. He also noted that the attack occurred in international waters.
Varna Regional Governor Mario Smurkov said there were no reports of injuries or fatalities among the crew. He told journalists that the sailors were conscious and that the Rescue Center had not reported any casualties, while acknowledging that they had likely experienced significant stress.
Smurkov praised the rescue effort by the Naval Forces and Border Police. The rescued crew members, all from the Philippines, were expected to undergo medical examinations before staying at a hotel arranged by the shipowner. The governor declined to discuss the cargo or possible environmental risks, but said the ship was listing heavily and there was no information indicating that it had sunk.
The Environment and Water Ministry reported that an initial inspection around Shabla and Bolata Bay, near Cape Kaliakra, had found no visible oil slicks, changes to the water surface or other apparent signs of pollution. The ministry said the findings were preliminary and would be supplemented by laboratory tests.
Teams from the Black Sea Basin Directorate and the Executive Environment Agency were scheduled to collect seawater samples from five coastal locations: Durankulak, Shabla, Cape Kaliakra, Byala and Sozopol. The samples will be tested for petroleum products, polychlorinated biphenyls, metals and other physicochemical indicators of water quality. Defense Ministry teams had already taken samples from two locations within Bulgaria’s territorial waters, and the Environment and Water Ministry said the results would be made public.
The CONTSHIP JET, built in 2007, was sailing under the Liberian flag from Haifa, Israel, to Constanța, Romania. The vessel is 160 meters long and 25 meters wide, and is managed by Greek companies, according to Equasis.
The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving aerial and maritime drones targeting commercial vessels near the Bulgarian and Romanian coasts during October. France had deployed an Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft to Romania’s Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base at Bucharest’s request because of the deteriorating security situation in the Black Sea. The aircraft has been conducting reconnaissance and surveillance missions in the western part of the sea from October 18 to November 6 to identify navigation hazards and improve protection of critical infrastructure in Romania’s exclusive economic zone.
The deployment forms part of NATO-backed deterrence operations and complements increased patrols by the Romanian Naval Forces using ships, helicopters and unmanned systems, along with warnings to mariners about hazards and recommended routes.
Separately, debris believed to belong to a Russian “Geran” combat drone was found along the coast near Arapya campsite, close to Tsarevo, according to a social media post by Alex Dimov of the podcast “Third of March 1918.” Dimov said photographs of the remains showed the inscription “Geran,” a designation used for Russian strike drones. The person who discovered the debris asked to remain anonymous, while Dimov said he could vouch for the source.
In his Facebook post, Dimov called for an investigation and public disclosure of the findings, raising questions about Bulgaria’s security and the response of the authorities. He also asked for the positions of Radev and Yotova, writing: "Bulgarian citizens deserve answers, transparency, and institutions that protect national security and uphold our country's commitments to our European allies!" He added: "Bulgarian national security is not open to compromise!"
In response to an inquiry from OffNews, the Defense Ministry press office said a team from the Burgas Naval Base had conducted an operation on October 21 to inspect and recover unmanned aerial vehicle debris found along the shoreline at Popski Beach in Tsarevo. The remains were transported to the naval base.

Putin says trade turnover with Egypt ‘growing steadily’ despite regional tensions

Burç Eruygur
28 October 2026•Update: 28 October 2026
President Vladimir Putin said Wednesday that Russia’s trade turnover with Egypt is “growing steadily” despite regional tensions, as he met Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Moscow.
In opening remarks during the talks, held on the sidelines of the two-day Russia-Africa summit that began in Moscow earlier Wednesday, Putin said joint efforts have accomplished a great deal since the first summit in 2019, as shown by the growth in trade between Russia and Africa.
“Since 2022, the total volume has increased by 50%, surpassing $27 billion. Egypt accounts for a significant portion of this trade turnover,” said Putin, noting that there is much “common ground” between Russia and the continent on development priorities.
Noting that, together with their colleagues, they will discuss the state and future prospects of Russia-Africa engagement and outline new areas for cooperation during plenary sessions Thursday, Putin noted their engagement on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi last month.
“The historic relationship between our two countries is rooted in the principles of mutual respect, consideration for each other’s interests and mutual assistance. These relations are developing successfully in accordance with the Treaty on Comprehensive Partnership and Strategic Cooperation,” he said.
Putin noted that trade turnover between Russia and Egypt continues to grow steadily “despite regional tensions,” stating that it has already increased 14% in the first eight months of 2026.
“In 2025, it reached record levels, exceeding $10 billion for the first time,” he said, praising the joint intergovernmental commission between the two countries.
“The flagship project, the construction of the El Dabaa Nuclear Power Plant in Egypt, is proceeding according to schedule. On July 9, a formal ceremony was held to mark the installation of the reactor pressure vessel for the second power unit,” he added.
Sisi said Egypt is working to develop the strategic partnership and hopes to expand cooperation, primarily in the economy and trade, as well as in areas related to grain supplies.
“Furthermore, the El Dabaa project remains the most significant initiative in our bilateral engagement,” said Sisi, noting they are committed to completing the projects according to the established timelines, and are making “every effort” to meet payment obligations.
He said he is counting on the Russian president's support to ensure they can deliver the El Dabaa project on schedule.
“We look forward to strengthening and broadening our cooperation. This includes the potential for installing new power units beyond 2030, as well as the development of a research reactor and a testing center,” he said.
Sisi added that they are also interested in collaborating with Russia on small-scale nuclear reactors, including floating nuclear power units, and in deepening their partnership within specialized industrial sectors, such as the extraction of uranium and rare metals.

Netanyahu opens coalition talks as opposition weighs bid to oust Knesset speaker
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:33:25 UTC
04:33:25 KST

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began talks with his political allies Wednesday following an inconclusive parliamentary election, speaking with far-right ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir as rival opposition leaders prepared their own consultations over the formation of the next government.
Netanyahu held his first post-election conversations with Finance Minister Smotrich, who leads the Religious Zionist Party, and National Security Minister Ben-Gvir, chairman of the far-right Otzma Yehudit party. Talks with leaders of the ultra-Orthodox parties are expected to follow.
The discussions marked the first steps toward coalition negotiations after Tuesday's election left neither Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc nor the rival pro-change alliance with enough seats to command a majority in the 120-member Knesset.
According to the Central Elections Committee, 88.6% of votes had been counted as of the latest update, with no change in the projected distribution of seats among the main political blocs.
Netanyahu's bloc was projected to win 53 seats, compared with 48 for the pro-change bloc and 19 for the predominantly Arab parties. A governing majority requires at least 61 seats.
The figures remain preliminary, with hundreds of thousands of ballots still outstanding.
The Central Elections Committee estimated that between 430,000 and 480,000 so-called double-envelope ballots had yet to be counted. These include votes cast by soldiers and other eligible voters outside their regular polling stations. Counting of those ballots had not yet begun.
"The processing work is in full swing, and not all the outer envelopes have yet been received," the committee said.
An analysis of the latest results also showed that the joint Reservists-Economic Party list, led by former minister Yoaz Hendel and economist Yaron Zelekha, remained 30,910 votes short of the electoral threshold required to enter parliament.
If the list crosses the threshold, it could alter the distribution of seats and further complicate efforts to form a government.
Opposition leaders prepare talks after day of silence
After nearly 24 hours without contact among leaders of the pro-change bloc, Democrats Chairman Yair Golan is expected to hold separate meetings Thursday with Yashar! leader Gadi Eisenkot and Yair Lapid of the Beyachad party.
No meeting has yet been scheduled between Golan and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who also leads Beyachad.
The consultations are expected to focus on the opposition's options following an election that left the bloc short of a parliamentary majority despite its efforts to unseat Netanyahu.
One of the first proposals likely to be discussed is replacing Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, a member of Netanyahu's Likud party, when the newly elected parliament convenes.
Although no concrete negotiations have begun, opposition figures are considering whether to move against Ohana as early as the Knesset's swearing-in ceremony, expected on Nov. 10.
The initiative would likely require support from predominantly Arab parties, whose combined parliamentary representation is projected to increase to 19 seats.
Opposition leaders view replacing the speaker as a parliamentary maneuver rather than a formal political alliance with Arab parties. Nevertheless, they recognize that relying on Arab lawmakers could carry a political cost.
Likud, for its part, is expected to portray any such effort as evidence that the pro-change bloc is joining forces with the Joint List, an alliance of predominantly Arab political factions.
There are also disagreements within the opposition over potential cooperation with Golan's leftist Democrats party, adding another complication to efforts to coordinate a common strategy.
Ultra-Orthodox party weighs abstention on speaker vote
United Torah Judaism, an ultra-Orthodox party traditionally aligned with Netanyahu, is considering abstaining if a vote to remove Ohana is brought before the new Knesset.
Such a move could affect the parliamentary arithmetic surrounding the opposition's initiative.
Tensions between Ohana and some ultra-Orthodox lawmakers are not new.
During the election campaign, United Torah Judaism lawmaker Yitzhak Pindrus criticized Ohana in an interview with the ultra-Orthodox newspaper Mishpacha.
Ohana's sexual orientation has drawn objections from some ultra-Orthodox politicians, who oppose homosexuality on religious grounds.
"The government failed because Amir Ohana was Knesset speaker. It was a desecration of God's name," Pindrus said.
Despite the possibility of abstaining on the speaker vote, United Torah Judaism has not announced any intention to leave Netanyahu's political bloc.
Party chairman Yaakov Asher said there had been no contacts between United Torah Judaism and the pro-change parties.
"We wish to clarify that there have been no approaches from party leaders, apart from a message conveyed by people close to Prime Minister Netanyahu indicating that he intends to keep the coalition parties together," Asher's office said.
Shas rules out abandoning Netanyahu
Another key ultra-Orthodox party, Shas, signaled that it would remain loyal to Netanyahu.
A Shas official told ynet that party chairman Aryeh Deri had no intention of abandoning the alliance he helped build or opening negotiations with Eisenkot.
"Anyone who thinks that Deri, the day after the election, will leave the bloc he established and start courting Eisenkot is very much mistaken," the official said.
The statement appeared intended to dispel speculation that Netanyahu's traditional religious allies might consider joining an alternative coalition.
With Netanyahu's bloc projected to hold 53 seats, the prime minister would need support from lawmakers outside his existing alliance to reach the 61-seat threshold.
Bennett urges supporters to remain hopeful
Bennett, whose Beyachad party was projected to win 12 seats before the counting of double-envelope ballots, acknowledged the disappointing results for the pro-change bloc but sought to encourage his supporters.
"My brothers and sisters, keep your heads up," Bennett wrote on X. "We have only one home, and we are here to stay. With God's help, things will be good here!"
He accompanied the post with a video thanking members of his party's election campaign staff.
The former prime minister has not publicly outlined a new coalition strategy, and no meeting with Golan has been arranged.

Israeli firm turned Starlink traffic into espionage tool across 105 countries
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:31:40 UTC
04:31:40 KST

Israeli firm turned Starlink traffic into espionage tool across 105 countries
Netanyahu loses his majority, Eisenkot cannot win one, and the wars go on
TEHRAN — Recent disclosures from digital defense watchdogs have exposed an obscure Tel Aviv-registered advertising company, Discover-Tech, running aggressive online ad campaigns designed to geolocate and track users of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet network across more than 100 countries.
Investigative research by TrendAI, a division of Tokyo-based Trend Micro, revealed that Discover-Tech became the dominant global bidder for ad space displayed to Starlink terminals, according to a Reuters report on Oct. 27.
Operating under the internal threat codenamed "Shadow-Earth-79," the Israeli firm captured an implausibly high share of ad auctions in restricted or conflict-heavy jurisdictions including Syria, Libya, Yemen, South Sudan, and Venezuela.
By harvesting the metadata embedded in real-time bidding requests, Discover-Tech systematically turned routine browser traffic into an active intelligence pipeline.
From ad impressions to silent infiltration
Programmatic ad auctions rely on instant exchanges of telemetry. Every time an advertisement loads on a web page or mobile application, a bid request transmits the user's IP address, device model, software configuration, autonomous system number, and exact location parameters to participating ad networks.
Discover-Tech leveraged this routine infrastructure to build a comprehensive tracking map.
TrendAI concluded that the firm’s bidding behavior reflected a dedicated tracking operation rather than commercial marketing, noting that legitimate Western advertising demand in heavily sanctioned states is virtually non-existent.
On observed Starlink connections, Discover-Tech accounted for nearly 13 percent of winning ad bids worldwide.
The surveillance mechanism went far beyond passive location mapping. Concurrent technical investigations by Canada’s Citizen Lab and ad-security firm Confiant exposed a sophisticated exploitation vector named "AdFection."
Discover-Tech's proprietary ad platform served as a conduit, connecting mainstream advertising exchanges directly to mercenary spyware operators. When a targeted device loaded a background advertisement, Discover-Tech servers screened the incoming telemetry.
High-value targets were served malicious JavaScript that delivered zero-click attack payloads without requiring any user interaction, while ordinary users received empty responses.
Citizen Lab confirmed with high confidence that at least 45 devices belonging to news personnel at Al Jazeera were targeted with Candiru spyware through this ad-driven vector.
Starlink and the military-industrial infrastructure
The focus on Starlink underscores how low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations have become central to Western military strategy and intelligence operations.
SpaceX's Starlink network bypasses land-based telecommunications gateways, routing data through satellite links to circumvent national regulatory frameworks and local internet blocks.
The U.S. Department of "War" and NATO forces have integrated Starlink and its military-grade derivative, Starshield, into frontline combat operations. In Ukraine, the technology provides primary battlefield command architecture, directing artillery, facilitating real-time satellite coordination, and guiding long-range combat drones.
This deep integration into Western military operations makes Starlink terminals prime targets for intelligence agencies.
Intelligence outfits seek to identify, geolocate, and compromise satellite terminals operating inside sensitive sovereign territory.
Israeli-owned firms were already pitching commercial clients on specialized methodologies to map and deanonymize Starlink subscribers by exploiting commercial ad data.
The Discover-Tech operation confirms that these theoretical pitches were already operationalized at a global scale, turning satellite terminals into beacons for military intelligence gathering.
The broader ecosystem of Israeli cyber warfare
Discover-Tech represents the latest evolution of a commercial cyber-arms ecosystem cultivated by the Israeli regime.
For decades, intelligence entities such as Unit 8200 and Mossad have maintained an institutional pipeline into private surveillance vendors, enabling former Israeli operatives to commercialize state-funded hacking techniques.
Discover-Tech’s corporate history shows direct ties to veteran surveillance executives, including past directors associated with Circles, an affiliate of NSO Group, and Senpai Technologies, linked to the Intellexa consortium.
This ecosystem includes a wide network of offensive vendors. NSO Group gained global infamy through its Pegasus software, which infected the phones of diplomats, political opponents, and human rights defenders.
Candiru, operating under various corporate names such as Saito Tech and Integrity Labs, specialized in zero-click desktop compromises. Paragon Solutions markets its Graphite interception software, while Intellexa and Cytrox developed the Predator spyware suite.
Other key players include Cognyte, Cytrox, Cellebrite, and Black Cube, the private intelligence agency staffed by former Israeli operatives specializing in deception and corporate espionage.
These entities routinely establish international shell companies across Europe to bypass nominal export restrictions and maintain access to global markets.
Industry self-censorship and structural vulnerability
Despite the scale of Discover-Tech’s operations, accountability remains hindered by self-censorship within the commercial security sector.
TrendAI initially omitted Discover-Tech’s name from its public report, opting instead for the "Shadow-Earth-79" alias after corporate executives raised legal concerns.
This practice allows offensive operators to evade immediate platform bans and legal scrutiny.
Following the public identification by Citizen Lab and news outlets, major tech platforms including Google, Comcast's Beeswax, Vungle, and Eskimi cut off Discover-Tech’s access, while IAB Europe suspended the firm from its approved vendor list.
Internal inquiries were also launched by a major U.S. technology corporation and an international organization to evaluate potential employee targeting.
These platform removals disrupt specific operational routes, but the underlying vulnerability remains unaddressed.
Discover-Tech operated inside approved industry registries for years, utilizing standard European data privacy frameworks to collect targeting parameters.
As long as commercial advertising exchanges permit real-time data harvesting, state-aligned surveillance contractors will continue to use programmatic ad bidding as an unregulated, low-cost vector for global espionage.

Tokayev says Türkiye among Kazakhstan’s five largest trading partners
The meeting between the Presidents of Kazakhstan and Türkiye continued with the participation of members of the official delegations of the two countries, Qazinform News Agency cites Akorda.
Kassym-Jomart Tokayev described the meeting as deeply symbolic, as it was being held on the eve of the Republic Day of Türkiye, and congratulated President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and the brotherly Turkish people on this significant national holiday.
“Under your wise leadership, Türkiye is successfully implementing large-scale reforms. The country is developing dynamically, pursuing political and economic modernization. Türkiye’s position on the international stage continues to grow stronger year by year. You are recognized as one of the world’s most influential leaders. Your principled and resolute political course, as well as your tireless efforts to uphold peace and justice, have earned global recognition. I am confident that the standing of the Turkish people will continue to grow. Kazakhstan unwaveringly supports Türkiye and sincerely rejoices in all the achievements of the brotherly Turkish people,” the President of Kazakhstan said.
Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized that he attaches particular importance to expanding cooperation with Türkiye.
“Relations between Kazakhstan and Türkiye have deep historical roots. We are united by our shared history and language, as well as similar traditions. Political interaction between our states rests on a solid foundation of mutual trust and enduring friendship. There are no contradictions or disagreements between us. Our countries consistently support each other both bilaterally and within international organizations. Trade and economic ties continue to expand steadily. Türkiye is one of Kazakhstan’s five largest trading partners. Furthermore, Türkiye ranks among the ten largest investors in our country, having made substantial investments in Kazakhstan’s economy. Many major Turkish companies operate successfully in Kazakhstan. We stand ready to provide comprehensive support to our Turkish partners and create favorable conditions for their businesses,” the Head of State said.
According to Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s state visit to Kazakhstan in May this year was highly productive and resulted in a number of important agreements. The sixth meeting of the High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council between the two countries was held. Major projects were launched in trade and economic cooperation, investment, and cultural and humanitarian affairs. Kazakhstan-Türkiye relations have reached the level of eternal friendship and enhanced strategic partnership.
“The steady development of our bilateral partnership serves our common interests. Tomorrow, we will attend the 13th Summit of the Organization of Turkic States together. The COP31 Climate Summit will be held in Antalya in the near future, and I intend to participate. These events will undoubtedly give fresh impetus to strengthening our bilateral and multifaceted ties,” Kassym-Jomart Tokayev noted.
In turn, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan congratulated the Head of State and the brotherly people of Kazakhstan on the recent Republic Day.
The Turkish President noted that a presentation of the book The Phenomenon of a Qurultay, dedicated to the history of Kazakh statehood, had recently been held in Ankara. In addition, the book Nauryz – A Common Heritage of the Turkic World, which comprehensively explores the history and significance of the holiday, has been translated into Kazakh.
“During my visit to Astana in May this year, we signed a number of important documents, including the Declaration on Eternal Friendship and Enhanced Strategic Partnership. We intend to reinforce our cooperation with practical steps at the next meeting of the Strategic Cooperation Council. We aim to increase bilateral trade to 15 billion US dollars and intensify the investment dimension of our relations,” the Turkish president said.
During the talks, the two sides also discussed prospects for cooperation in transport and logistics, energy, artificial intelligence, agriculture, and the defense industry, as well as ways to strengthen cultural and humanitarian ties.
Earlier, Qazinform reported Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan had held restricted-format talks.

92-year-old US judge handling Nicolas Maduro case dies
NEW YORK - Alvin Hellerstein, the US judge overseeing the case against deposed Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro, has died aged 92, an official confirmed on Oct 28.
As one of the oldest US federal judges, questions had been raised about whether he was the right justice to preside over what could be a prolonged trial for Maduro on drug trafficking charges.
Hellerstein’s lengthy career included overseeing the civil cases arising from Al-Qaeda’s Sept 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on New York and Washington, often rejecting deals he saw as unfair to complainants.
His death was confirmed to AFP by an official at the United States District Court, Southern District of New York, where he presided.
A court filing showed the case has been reassigned to Analisa Torres, born in 1959.
Hellerstein also tangled with Donald Trump, rejecting a request by the US president to have his New York hush money case moved to federal court.
In 2025, he blocked the Trump administration from deporting alleged Venezuelan gang members without a court hearing.
In a noteworthy 2015 ruling, Hellerstein ordered the US government to release a trove of photos depicting abuse of detainees in Iraq and Afghanistan.
He also presided over a trial in 2025 in which a jury found French banking giant BNP Paribas’ work in Sudan had helped prop up the regime of former ruler Omar al-Bashir, awarding US$20.75 million (S$26 million) in damages to three plaintiffs from Sudan.
Hellerstein handled the sprawling drug trafficking case linked to Maduro for over a decade, which has already seen the conviction of Venezuela’s former intelligence chief, Hugo Armando Carvajal.
Maduro was seized by US forces in January, in a military raid on his compound in Venezuela.
A graduate of Columbia University law school, Hellerstein served as a lawyer in the US Army from 1957 to 1960 before entering private practice.
He was nominated by then president Bill Clinton in 1998 to be a district court judge for the Southern District of New York. AFP

Costa Rica drops bid to join Pacific trade pact, sacks trade minister
- Costa Rica has withdrawn its bid to join the CPTPP after protests from producer groups, especially farmers, over the secretive deal.
- President Laura Fernandez said trade minister Indiana Trejos was sacked for “lack of transparency” after helping with talks under the previous government.
- Costa Rica had applied in 2022, held over 100 meetings, and was invited in November 2024, but the government now says almost no one knows what the pact entails.
AI generated
SAN JOSE - Costa Rica's government has withdrawn its bid to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), a major trans-Pacific trade pact, and dismissed its foreign trade minister, president Laura Fernandez said on Oct 28.
Fernandez said the removal of foreign trade minister Indiana Trejos, who had participated in the negotiations as deputy minister during the previous administration, was due to lack of transparency. The president did not say who is due to replace Trejos.
The decision to scrap the application comes after protests from Costa Rica's producer groups, especially from the agriculture sector.
The CPTPP is a free trade bloc of 12 nations across the Americas, Asia, Oceania and Europe that accounts for nearly 15% of global gross domestic product.
“Although it might seem like an excellent opportunity, its full content was declared secret by the negotiators to the point that almost no one knows what it entails,” Fernandez said in a video posted on social media.
Costa Rica submitted a request to join the CPTPP in 2022 and held more than 100 high-level meetings to build consensus among members. In November 2024 the bloc formally invited the Central American country form part of the CPTPP.
Since then, Costa Rica has reviewed its regulations against the agreement's rules and negotiated market access for goods and services.
The CPTPP went into effect in 2018 as an offshoot of the Trans-Pacific Partnership, following the United States' departure from that proposed trade bloc. REUTERS

Ukraine Develops Armored Evacuation Module for Murakha UGV
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:24:53 UTC
04:24:53 KST

Ukrainian company Robotic Complexes is developing a specialized CASEEVAK module for the Murakha unmanned ground vehicle (UGV).
The project is designed to protect wounded military personnel during transport and provide communications and monitoring of their condition, the company told Militarnyi.
Unlike conventional cargo UGVs, the new system features an armored capsule made of 3.5 mm Armox 500T steel with an internal HDPE 1000 lining.
The capsule is equipped with ventilation, heating and lighting systems, as well as a first-aid kit. Side and rear doors allow the wounded to be loaded from any side and provide access to them during evacuation.
A camera with day and night channels and two-way audio communication are installed inside to monitor the occupant’s condition.
The system is controlled through ELRS, LTE, Starlink or fiber-optic communication links. If the capsule is detached from the main platform, it retains two independent communication channels.
The developers are currently working to integrate vital-sign monitoring systems. This will allow medical personnel to receive information about the casualty’s condition while the vehicle is moving.
The platform’s protection is supplemented by passive counter-drone measures, net launchers and electronic warfare systems. An electric powertrain has been installed to reduce the vehicle’s signature.
The platform has two electric motors with a combined torque of 1,600 N·m and a 35 kWh battery pack. Its range is up to 80 km.
Company specialists have already conducted ballistic tests of the armor steel at a distance of 50 meters using various calibers. Development of a slat armor system to protect against FPV drones is also underway.
Militarnyi previously reported that in October 2025, Ukrainian forces began using Murakha-Mini ground drones to support logistics near the front line.
The UGVs help deliver equipment, food and other supplies.

inside the parisian hotel renovation where british club culture meets haussmannian architecture
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:24:01 UTC
04:24:01 KST

inside the parisian hotel renovation where british club culture meets haussmannian architecture
at paris’ historic hotel westminster, laurent maugoust renovates the historic interiors while helen stephens reimagines the restaurant, preserving two centuries of architectural heritage.
prefer designboom on google
[FEATURED]
FROM NAPOLEON’S PARIS TO A BRITISH HOTEL
In a city with no shortage of historic hotels, Hotel Westminster has had more than two centuries to develop its identity. Located at 13 rue de la Paix, between Place Vendôme and the Palais Garnier, the Parisian address has undergone an extensive restoration led by interior architect Laurent Maugoust, with British designer Helen Stephens reimagining its restaurant, Le Céladon. The project, completed one year ago, preserves architectural elements accumulated throughout the building’s history while introducing contemporary interiors. Awarded its fifth star in 2025, the Westminster enters its latest chapter with a rather unusual distinction: a distinctly British character in one of the most recognizably French corners of Paris.
The story begins in 1802, when Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the sale of land belonging to a former Capuchin convent and commissioned architects Percier and Fontaine to develop a new district. The street, originally named rue Napoléon before becoming rue de la Paix in 1814, welcomed the Hôtel Wagram in 1807, the predecessor of today’s Westminster. As British travelers increasingly settled in the neighborhood, the area acquired the reputation of being a small piece of London in Paris, an identity reflected in the hotel’s eventual name. The building itself continued to evolve through successive extensions and renovations, most notably between 1905 and 1907, when architect Jacques Marcel Aubertin gave it the Haussmannian silhouette it retains today.
LAURENT MAUGOUST RESTORES HAUSSMANNIAN INTERIORS
For Laurent Maugoust, the restoration involved working with architectural elements belonging to different periods rather than recreating a single historical moment. Across the hotel’s 102 rooms, including 20 suites, the intervention preserves marble fireplaces, decorative mouldings and herringbone oak parquet floors, combining them with contemporary furnishings and textiles in shades of beige, green and violet. The designer’s approach draws on his experience with Haussmannian interiors, where proportions, materials and craftsmanship establish a continuity between past and present. ‘I set out to reinterpret its style by bringing different eras into dialogue,’ Maugoust explains, describing a project that builds on the existing architecture rather than attempting to replace it.
Other details reveal how the Westminster has accumulated its own collection of objects and decorative elements over the decades. Antique clocks, some dating from the 19th century, remain scattered throughout the rooms and suites, alongside paintings, historical photographs and furnishings associated with the property’s past. Some suites overlook rue de la Paix, while others face a flower-filled inner courtyard, offering two rather different perspectives on central Paris. These surviving features also reflect the building’s long history of transformation, from its early extensions to the reconstruction that established its present appearance. At the Westminster, even the supposedly timeless Haussmannian setting has undergone more than a few changes.
DUKE’S BAR PRESERVES THE HOTEL’S BRITISH HERITAGE
The hotel’s most recognizable connection to Britain survives at Duke’s Bar, an English-club-inspired interior defined by dark wood panelling, deep armchairs, subdued lighting and an original fireplace. During the 1920s, the bar became a gathering place for British aristocrats and political figures, later attracting writers and personalities from Parisian cultural life. According to the hotel’s historical account, Winston Churchill was among its regular visitors, while Coco Chanel, Agatha Christie, Arthur Conan Doyle and Françoise Sagan also frequented the address. Black-and-white portraits of Churchill, Chanel, Rudyard Kipling and the Duke of Westminster now line the walls, preserving something of the atmosphere that once made the bar a meeting point between British and French society.
A different interpretation of the hotel’s history unfolds at Le Céladon, redesigned by Helen Stephens to establish a visual connection with Duke’s Bar. Shades of green reference both the bronze of the Vendôme Column and the foliage of the nearby Tuileries Garden, bringing elements of the surrounding city into the restaurant’s interiors. Beyond the dining spaces, the Westminster continues its relationship with Parisian cultural life through musical evenings and literary events organized in collaboration with Galignani, the city’s historic English-language bookshop. More than two centuries after the first hotel opened on rue de la Paix, the Westminster remains a curious meeting point between Parisian architecture and British tradition, two identities that have become difficult to separate.

Each of the three options facing US in confrontation with Iran carries strategic losses
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-28
19:23:09 UTC
04:23:09 KST

Each of the three options facing US in confrontation with Iran carries strategic losses
LONDON - America's available options in the West Asia region are constrained by substantial strategic costs, meaning that none appears to be free of losses. These options can be summarized in three main scenarios: maintaining a state of neither war nor peace, withdrawing without an agreement, or withdrawing under an agreement.
Maintaining a state of neither war nor peace involves maintaining the current situation without reaching a final settlement and without returning to open warfare at the same intensity.
The first option of maintaining a state of “neither war nor peace” does not mean that Iran’s instruments of pressure will cease to operate. If Iran continues working to break its blockade and retains the ability to target vessels or assets connected to the confrontation, Washington will find itself facing a prolonged war of attrition rather than a stable situation that can be managed without cost.
Maintaining the situation in this form may not be sustainable for more than two years, that is, until the end of Trump’s term, although this timeframe remains a political estimate rather than an established certainty.
The second option is “withdrawal without an agreement”. The United States may withdraw without reaching a comprehensive agreement, while maintaining its policy of sanctions against Iran.
In such a situation Iran will retain its right to respond effectively to the instruments of blockade. Its response could go beyond the methods used before the war.
Iran would continue working to break the naval blockade and impose costs on the countries maintaining it. This could include economic and political pressure and extend to military action if circumstances will warrant it.
This would leave the region in an unstable condition and force the U.S. to pull out of the region without a settlement, a step that postpones the conflict, rather than addressing its underlying causes. Iran would then gain additional strategic advantages on top of those it had already acquired through the war, including experience and the ability to shift the confrontation to another level, one in which the balance would be more favorable to Iran.
However, the consequences of a prolonged state of “neither war nor peace” for the global economy, commercial activity, financial markets and fertilizer supplies would create intense pressure to end the war. Such an outcome would not serve American interests, given that the United States would be regarded as responsible for initiating the illegitimate war on Iran.
This would significantly weaken American influence and international standing, as the country would be seen as a source of instability and negative repercussions, having drawn dozens of countries and entangled them in the consequences of a reckless war.
The third option of “withdrawal under an agreement” would allow the United States to end the confrontation on the basis of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding that contains 14 clauses. An agreement would pose a dilemma for the U.S. since the issue is not simply about money, but about the changes that an agreement could bring to the nature of Iran’s relationship with the wider region.
If Iran were integrated into regional political and economic relationships, the effectiveness of the terminology and policies used to isolate it could diminish. 
 
Furthermore, the normalization of economic and political relations could give Iran’s allies greater room to operate within recognized regional arrangements, rather than remaining under pressure and confrontation.
This could strengthen Iran’s regional position, consolidate the position of Ansarallah in Yemen and strengthen the Lebanese resistance's position. At the same time, the Israeli occupation entity could withdraw from the areas it entered following the war that began on February 28 in accordance with the first clause of the memorandum of understanding. If this outcome is materialized as described, it would represent more than a ceasefire. It would amount to a restructuring of the regional balance of power and political relationships.
Withdrawal without an agreement could leave Iran under naval blockade but it would fail to bring Iran under American control, yet withdrawal under an agreement could provide Iran with extensive economic and political opportunities. Maintaining the current situation would also leave America facing continuous attrition. This leads to the argument that all three options, despite their differences, carry strategic losses for the United States.
